label: Senusret I builds the first large stone temple
was: Senusret I builds the first stone temple
more: Senusret I (reigned about 1965 to 1920 BC) built a limestone temple for Amun-Ra, about 38 metres square, with a portico of Osiris pillars and red granite doorsills. It replaced smaller Eleventh Dynasty buildings, so it was the first large stone temple, not the first.

label: Thutmose III begins the Akhmenu
more: Thutmose III began the Akhmenu, 'the most glorious of monuments', after his twenty-third year, behind what was then Karnak's east wall. It took about seven years and probably marks his jubilee. It holds the tent-pole hall, Sokar rooms, a sun court and the botanical room.

label: Lateran obelisk shipped to Rome
more: The lone obelisk of east Karnak, begun by Thutmose III and raised by Thutmose IV, was taken to Alexandria in the fourth century. Constantius II had it set up in Rome's Circus Maximus in 357. It was re-erected at the Lateran in 1588.

label: Temple closed; churches in the ruins
more: Pagan worship was banned across the Roman empire in the late fourth century and Karnak was largely abandoned. Christians built churches among the ruins, the best known in the Akhmenu's central hall, where painted saints survive. Exact dates are uncertain.
